limitations: caller_scope is caller/session provenance, changes when the downstream client key rotates, and is not a Canonical APIKeyID.

decisions.failureBehavior: Missing or ambiguous caller_scope must remain unknown and must not be bound as a Canonical APIKeyID.
decisions.fallback: Phase3 creates independent Canonical APIKeyID and CredentialID values, retains source provenance, and redacts raw credentials at adapter boundaries.

limitations: Candidate v7.3.8 preserves the same caller_scope rotation and lifecycle limits as v7.3.3.

decisions.failureBehavior: Missing or ambiguous caller_scope must remain unknown and must not be promoted from candidate evidence.

limitations: The scheduler sees only the highest available priority tier in v7.3.3.
A target must remain in CPA's eligible candidate set and cannot bypass provider, model, authorization, disabled, or cooldown filters.
An invalid scheduler Auth.ID falls back to the built-in selector, so that response is not proof of hard routing.
Streaming does not gain the same retry/reselection behavior as non-stream execution.
decisions.failureBehavior: A product hard-route request must use pinned_auth_id and fail closed when the eligible target is unavailable; invalid scheduler fallback must never be reported as target success.
decisions.fallback: Disable the hard-route action or present highest-tier-only eligibility; do not silently select a different credential for an explicit target.

limitations: v7.3.8 default configuration remains restricted to the highest available priority tier.
The accepted default-config machine records prove highest-tier visibility, valid/invalid scheduler handling, and pinned target fencing; they do not inherit the opt-in pre-filter record.
Streaming retry/reselection remains stage-limited.
decisions.failureBehavior: Explicit target selection must fail closed through pinned_auth_id; default scheduler fallback cannot satisfy a hard-route promise.
decisions.fallback: Keep the candidate in evidence-only status and expose only the verified highest-tier boundary.

limitations: Across-priority visibility is available only with the explicit v7.3.8 opt-in.
Pre-scheduler eligibility filtering still applies to every target.
Invalid scheduler responses still fall back and stream retry remains limited.
The candidate is not the bundled runtime.
decisions.failureBehavior: Unknown, filtered, disabled, cooldown, or otherwise ineligible targets must fail closed; a built-in fallback must not be called hard routing.
decisions.fallback: Remain on the current bundle or disable across-priority routing until a separate bundle/release acceptance enables this exact configuration.

limitations: RequestID identifies one model request lifecycle and is not an attempt identifier.
Paths rejected before tracker creation do not produce this correlation.
decisions.failureBehavior: Events without a directly observed RequestID remain uncorrelated; no synthetic RequestID may be inferred after the fact.
decisions.fallback: Store the observation as unknown/unlinked while preserving any independent transport trace metadata.

limitations: Candidate RequestID continuity does not add attempt identity.
Candidate evidence does not authorize a product bundle upgrade.
decisions.failureBehavior: Unobserved RequestID values remain uncorrelated and cannot be reconstructed from the candidate fixture.
decisions.fallback: Use the current supported RequestID contract only after exact artifact/config negotiation.

limitations: Retries share RequestID and overwrite selected_auth metadata without a stable AttemptID or ordinal.
UsageRecord lacks RequestID, AttemptID, and an idempotency key.
decisions.failureBehavior: Do not reconstruct attempt history from final metadata or callback order.
decisions.fallback: Expose request-level evidence only and mark per-attempt correlation unavailable.

publishAttemptRecord does not supply a stable cross-callback attempt identity.
decisions.failureBehavior: Do not infer an attempt ledger from callback count or selected_auth metadata.
decisions.fallback: Keep per-attempt policy and settlement disabled until the upstream contract exists.

limitations: Tracked requests invoke terminal completion once, but pre-tracker rejections emit none.
Plugin failure, fuse, reload, or unavailability can drop the asynchronous notification.
decisions.failureBehavior: Missing terminal notification is unknown coverage, not proof that a request did not happen.
decisions.fallback: Retain bounded freshness/coverage state and reconcile with independent usage or operation evidence when available.

limitations: Candidate terminal cardinality is exactly once only for requests that created a tracker.
Candidate delivery remains in-memory and can be lost on plugin lifecycle failures.
decisions.failureBehavior: Missing candidate callbacks remain unknown and cannot be promoted to reliable delivery.
decisions.fallback: Use the same bounded coverage model as v7.3.3; do not treat candidate evidence as durable delivery.

limitations: Completed usage can support observed/notify behavior but is asynchronous and best effort.
Streaming cancellation may produce partial or zero-token records.
Retries and additional-model records can produce multiple callbacks without exact request/attempt keys.
decisions.failureBehavior: Missing, late, duplicate, or uncorrelated usage must lower freshness/coverage and must never authorize a hard cap.
decisions.fallback: Expose observed/notify state with explicit freshness, coverage, and unknown semantics.

limitations: v7.3.8 preserves best-effort usage observation without exact request/attempt correlation.

decisions.failureBehavior: Missing, late, duplicate, or uncorrelated candidate usage remains unknown coverage and cannot authorize hard enforcement.
decisions.fallback: Retain observed/notify behavior after exact artifact/config acceptance only.

limitations: There is no persistent exactly-once usage delivery, first-class reservation, or authoritative settlement primitive.
Generic RequestInterceptResponse.Terminate is not proof of concurrency-safe token or cost quota enforcement.

decisions.fallback: Use Phase5 R1 observed/notify behavior; evaluate any soft or request-count gate as a separate metric-specific task.

limitations: v7.3.8 still lacks persistent exactly-once delivery, reservation, rollback, and idempotent settlement.

decisions.failureBehavior: Candidate precise token/cost hard quota must remain disabled and cannot justify a bundle upgrade.
decisions.fallback: Retain observed/notify semantics and wait for metric-specific upstream capability plus separate acceptance.

limitations: External runtime version, artifact identity, Plugin ABI, enabled config, and capability generation are not negotiated.

decisions.fallback: Keep management-plane compatibility without capability claims until an exact negotiation and independent compatibility acceptance succeeds.
